chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajistani the judge informed me, saying: Ibn Sa'id informed us, saying: Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan and Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn Sayyar narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ayyub ibn Atbah narrated to us, from al-Fadl ibn Bakir al-Abdi, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

He said: There are three things that destroy and three things that save. As for the three that save, they are: fearing Allah, the Exalted, in private and in public; moderation in wealth and poverty; and justice in pleasure and anger. And as for the three that destroy, they are: a widely obeyed stinginess, which is followed; and a person's admiration for themselves. And another hadith has been narrated from the Imam (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Widely obeyed stinginess is having a bad opinion of Allah, the Exalted.' And I have presented it with its chain of narration in the book Ma'ani al-Akhbar.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that destroy and the three things that save according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal outlines the spiritual anatomy of the self, contrasting the 'three destroyers'—insatiable greed, blind following of desires, and self-admiration—with the 'three saviors' rooted in God-consciousness, moderation, and emotional justice. Imam al-Sadiq’s clarification that stinginess stems from a 'bad opinion of God' (su' al-zann bi-Allah) deepens the psychological insight, linking material attachment to theological perception. This framework serves as a practical guide for ethical self-purification (tazkiyah) in Shia moral theology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-11 The judge al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sejezy narrated that Ibn Sa’ed quoted Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qat’tan and Ahmad ibn Mansoor ibn Sayyar, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Yunus, on the authority of Ayoob ibn Atabat, on the authority of Al-Fazl ibn Bakir al-Abdi , on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“There are three things which destroy and three things which save. As for the three things which save, they are fearing the Honorable the Exalted God in private and in public; moderation in times of poverty and affluence; and speaking fairly whether you are pleased or angry. As for the three things which destroy, they are being really stingy; following one’s selfish desires; and being haughty and selfish.”In another tradition that has been narrated on the authority of Imam as-Sadiq (MGB), we read, “Being really stingy implies being suspicious of the Honorable the Exalted God.” I have presented the chain of narrations of this tradition in the book Ma’ani al-Akhbar.
